'''David John Honey''' (born 18 April 1958) is an Australian politician who was the [[Western Australian Liberal Party|Liberal Party]] member for the [[electoral district of Cottesloe]] in the [[Western Australian Legislative Assembly]] from 2018 to 2025. He was leader of the WA Liberal Party from March 2021 until he was defeated in a [[2023 Western Australian Liberal Party leadership spill|leadership spill in January 2023]], and was previously the Shadow Minister for Industrial Development, Water and Lands, and the Liberal Party's Legislative Assembly Policy Co-ordinator. He was defeated in [[preselection]] by [[Sandra Brewer]], who succeeded him as the member for Cottesloe.

==Education and early career==
Honey completed a Bachelor of Science with first-class Honours and a PhD in Chemistry at the University of Western Australia, as well as being the UWA Science Union President. He has held technical roles including as a Forensic Scientist and Environmental Scientist with the State Government, and also formed the Hydrometallurgy Research Group for Western Australian Mining Corporation.

Honey was formerly the Global Residue Manager for Alcoa's Refining operations, having overall accountability for the refining residue operations in the United States, Spain, Brazil and Australia. Prior to that role, Honey held senior management and technical roles in Alcoa. He joined Alcoa as a Senior Principal Research Scientist in the Global Refining Centre of Excellence before moving on to the positions of Clarification Manager, Pinjarra Refinery, Digestion manager, Kwinana Refinery, Production Manager, Kwinana Refinery, and Western Australian Operations Residue Manager.

From 2012 to 2018, he was the President of the Kwinana Industries Council, a lobby group representing chemical, petroleum, cement and other firms in Kwinana.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kwinana Industries Council|url=https://kic.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/KIC-Annual-Report_RS_-2020.pdf|title=Annual Report 2020|year=2020}}</ref>

==Political career==
From 1994 to 1997, Honey was president of [[Liberal Party of Australia (Western Australian Division)|WA Liberal Party]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Our History |url=https://www.waliberal.org.au/our-history/ |publisher=WA Liberal Party |access-date=2021-03-22}}</ref> During that time, he was aligned with controversial Liberal Party power broker [[Noel Crichton-Browne]], but when Crichton-Browne made inappropriate sexual comments to journalist [[Colleen Egan]] at a Liberal Party conference in July 1995, Honey initiated the successful motion to expel Crichton-Browne from the party.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crichton-Browne, Noel Ashley (1944– ) |url=http://biography.senate.gov.au/crichton-browne-noel-ashley/ |website=The Biographical Dictionary of the Australian Senate |access-date=2021-03-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Transcript of the prime minister, the Hon P.J Keating MP doorstop, Sheraton Breakwater Casino-Hotel, Townsville, Monday, 14 August 1995 |url=https://pmtranscripts.pmc.gov.au/release/transcript-9705 |website=PM Transcripts |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=2021-03-22}}</ref> Honey later explained in March 2021, that as the party president, he had to deal with the issue of Crichton-Browne being a power broker and his "undue influence" over the party and preselections.

Honey was elected to the [[Western Australian Legislative Assembly]] in the [[2018 Cottesloe state by-election|Cottesloe by-election]] on 17 March 2018, following the resignation of former Premier [[Colin Barnett]]. At the [[2021 Western Australian state election|2021 state election]], Honey was one of only two Liberals to hold their seats in the massive landslide victory by the Labor Party, and the only non-Labor MP from Perth. The other Liberal member, [[Libby Mettam]], declined to contest the party leadership, leaving the position open for Honey when the party's parliamentary wing met to elect a leader on 23 March 2021.<ref name="lib leader">{{cite news |title=David Honey set to become leader of WA Liberals |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-03-22/david-honey-set-to-become-leader-of-wa-liberals/100022216 |access-date=22 March 2021 |work=ABC News |date=22 March 2021 |language=en-AU}}</ref> Upon his election as leader, Honey brought up his role in the expulsion of Crichton-Browne in 1995 as a reason why he should be leader of what remained of the WA Liberals, and vowed to oversee a "root and branch" analysis and restructuring of the party.<ref name="leadercb">{{cite news |title=WA Liberals seek formal coalition with Nationals as party confronts 'huge job' after election disaster |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-03-23/wa-liberals-seek-coalition-with-nationals-david-honey-new-leader/100023008 |access-date=23 March 2021 |work=ABC News |date=23 March 2021 |language=en-AU}}</ref>

In January 2023, Honey was challenged for the leadership by Mettam. Honey pulled out of [[2023 Liberal Party of Australia (Western Australian Division) leadership spill|the leadership contest]] on 30 January and Mettam replaced him as party leader unopposed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Perpitch |first1=Nicolas |last2=Bourke |first2=Keane |last3=Burmas |first3=Grace |title=Shane Love is WA's new opposition leader, as Libby Mettam takes over Liberal party leadership |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-01-30/david-honey-libby-mettam-wa-liberal-leadership/101904478 |website=ABC News |access-date=30 January 2023 |date=30 January 2023}}</ref>

In February 2024, Honey lost a Liberal party [[preselection]] ballot for the seat of Cottesloe to [[Sandra Brewer]], the head of the state's Property Council.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Spagnolo |first1=Joe |title=Sandra Brewer wins Cottesloe Liberal preselection, ending David Honey's reign |url=https://thewest.com.au/politics/state-politics/d-day-for-cottesloe-mp-david-honey-as-liberals-decide-preselection-c-13526701 |website=The West Australian |access-date=10 February 2024 |date=10 February 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Peppiatt |first1=Rebecca |last2=Hastie |first2=Hamish |title=David Honey out, Sandra Brewer selected as Liberal party's Cottesloe candidate |url=https://www.watoday.com.au/national/western-australia/david-honey-out-sandra-brewer-selected-as-liberal-party-s-cottesloe-candidate-20240210-p5f3wx.html |website=WAtoday |access-date=10 February 2024 |date=10 February 2024}}</ref>

===Political views===
In his maiden speech to parliament, Honey criticised plans for higher density housing in his electorate of Cottesloe, saying that places further out from the Perth CBD should be densified instead, such as [[Fremantle]] or [[Rockingham, Western Australia|Rockingham]]. Honey said that "Cottesloe is already doing more than its fair share" and "allowing [[Gold Coast, Queensland|Gold Coast]]-style high-rise on the beachfront would substantially diminish the attractiveness of this area for residents and visitors alike, including tourists".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carmody |first1=James |title=Cottesloe already doing enough to increase residential density, new Liberal MP says |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-04-13/cottesloe-mp-david-honey-urban-density/9651976 |website=ABC News |access-date=3 January 2024 |date=13 April 2018}}</ref> The issue of higher-density development has come up again in late-2023 due to the preselection challenge to Honey by Sandra Brewer.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bourke |first1=Keane |title=Property Council boss Sandra Brewer to challenge David Honey in WA Liberals' safest seat of Cottesloe |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-12-07/sandra-brewer-challenges-david-honey-liberal-seat-cottesloe/103200344 |website=ABC News |access-date=3 January 2024 |date=7 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Hastie |first1=Hamish |title=Property Council boss puts hand up in race for Cottesloe preselection |url=https://www.watoday.com.au/politics/western-australia/property-council-boss-puts-hand-up-in-race-for-cottesloe-preselection-20231207-p5epsw.html |website=WAtoday |access-date=3 January 2024 |date=7 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=McGinn |first1=Jack |title=Honey fires shot at Cott density |url=https://www.businessnews.com.au/article/Honey-fires-shot-at-Cott-density |website=Business News |access-date=3 January 2024 |date=3 January 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Honey's opponents have labelled him a [[NIMBY]], but he rejects the label, saying that "the term NIMBY (Not in my backyard) is an insulting slur meant to delegitimise the very real and reasonable concerns of local residents who care more about their community’s amenities and character than maximising profit for a developer".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dietsch |first1=Jake |title=Cottesloe MP Dr David Honey hits back at 'NIMBY slur' with American Chopper meme |url=https://thewest.com.au/news/wa/cottesloe-mp-dr-david-honey-hits-back-at-nimby-slur-with-american-chopper-meme-c-13405593 |website=The West Australian |access-date=10 February 2024 |date=30 January 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
